title: Read staffing, call summaries and unit response reports
summary: Run staffing and call reports with deliberate date and group scopes, inspect the actual detail tables and timestamp sources, and download a unit-row CSV without treating missing data as zero.
prerequisites: Use an authorized reporting account in a fictional practice department with existing calls and staffing history.
Check the department time zone and choose a deliberate report period; preserve operational data and existing staffing.
Use only fictional training records for practice and share downloaded results with authorized recipients.

sector_examples.Chicago Fire: Run a station-scoped call summary for a fixed exercise period, then inspect the matching unit times before describing response totals.
sector_examples.Community care and mental health: Review operational call workload in an agreed period without adding client histories or treating software timestamps as an assessment.
sector_examples.Search and rescue: Compare mission-period call groups using the same boundaries and distinguish missing unit times from recorded zero-duration activity.
sector_examples.Security: Review current recorded staffing and a bounded patrol call period; do not equate the staffing chart with attendance.
sector_examples.Wildland: Compare a defined seasonal window and its group scope; treat partial-period and future zero rows explicitly.
sector_examples.Industrial response: Inspect a training call’s unit-status chronology and preserve missing fields in a CSV used for an internal software exercise.

scenes.title: Choose the report for the question
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: Reports brings several questions together: who is currently staffed, what happened on calls, and which timestamps have been recorded. In our fictional Chicago Fire department, begin with the Reporting catalog. Find Staffing Report and use its View Report button. The report groups people by their latest recorded staffing level and provides a count and chart. Truck 81 has people in Available, Unavailable and On Shift categories. This is a staffing summary; it does not establish who physically attended an incident.
scenes.practice: Open Staffing Report and identify one group with more than one recorded staffing category.
source_limits: Only the catalog top is pictured. The Call Summary and Call Unit Times catalog launchers are below this viewport; their later scenes start on their actual parameter pages. A catalog link is not proof its report ran.

Bottom detail headers are clipped; use006. The chart is a genuine rendered staffing chart, not a Call Summary chart. Staffing is latest recorded software staffing, not attendance or crew-seat verification.

scenes.title: Check totals against types and states
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: The resulting header repeats the selected period. This captured run contains fifteen calls, with four open, nine unit responses and four personnel responses. Response totals accumulate across calls; they are not a count of unique department members or vehicles. The tables provide a useful cross-check. Investigation, Structure Fire, Rescue and Medical counts total fifteen. Call States separates eleven Closed from four Active. Read the table labels and denominators before comparing percentages with another report.

scenes.title: Understand how calls are assigned to groups
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: Calls by Group explains why a call belongs to a reporting group. Each call counts once. A containing group geofence is used first; otherwise the report uses the group associated with most dispatched resources. Some calls can remain unassigned. This is different from simply listing the current viewer’s group. Here, Firehouse 51 has seven calls and Command has five. Use the explanation when investigating a surprising group total instead of changing memberships to make a report match expectations.
scenes.practice: Read the Calls by Group explanation and identify the five calls attributed to Command.
source_limits: Help and group table are actual. Group attribution is not simply current viewer membership. Dispatch fallback can leave a call unassigned, including an even split.

scenes.title: Set the Call Unit Times window
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: Call Unit Times answers a more specific question: which dispatch and status timestamps exist for each unit on each call? Its parameter form has start and end times and Run Report. Here the range starts October twenty-fourth at twenty-three thirty and ends October twenty-ninth at twenty-three thirty. That begins thirty minutes earlier than our first Call Summary. Keep those periods distinct when reconciling the results.
scenes.practice: Read the Unit Times start and end and identify the thirty-minute difference from the earlier summary.

scenes.title: Interpret timestamps and their linkage
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
required_labels: No unit was dispatched to this call or reported a status on it.
scenes.narration: The generated report has Dispatched, En Route, On Scene, Staging, Cleared and Linked By columns. The original DEMO rows say Dispatch only and leave later status times blank. A dispatch entry alone does not establish an arrival. Other exercise rows say Unit status. Read the recorded timestamps as they stand; some are incomplete or out of order, so review the underlying history before calculating a duration. Some calls explicitly report no unit dispatch or status data. The native exercise shows Ambulance 61 with dispatch and en-route times, while its later cells remain blank. These are software records, not independent physical-arrival verification.
scenes.practice: Compare a Dispatch only row with a Unit status row without filling any blank timestamp.
source_limits: Original dispatch-only rows have blank En Route/On Scene/Staging/Cleared fields. Blank means missing timestamp, not zero or a verified nonresponse. Download CSV is an actual visible control.

FD0003 records En Route18:23:07, On Scene18:23:49 and Dispatched18:27:19; do not repair chronology or claim all fields are sequential. Current labels describe linked software records, not physical arrival.
Some calls have an explicit no-unit-data message;0008 has Ambulance61 and Unit status linkage with blank later fields. Do not count no-unit messages as exported unit rows.

scenes.title: Download and interpret the real CSV
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: Use Download CSV on this report to obtain its unit rows for the same parameters. The downloaded file includes call and unit identifiers, timestamps and Linked By. This exercise export contains thirteen unit rows for twelve distinct calls: a call with two units creates two rows, while a call with no unit rows contributes none. The file uses DispatchOnly and Explicit codes where the screen says Dispatch only and Unit status. Keep blank times blank, and retain the report period with your file.
scenes.practice: Download the CSV and compare one DispatchOnly row with the matching report row; retain blank cells.
source_limits: Original dispatch-only rows have blank En Route/On Scene/Staging/Cleared fields. Blank means missing timestamp, not zero or a verified nonresponse. Download CSV is an actual visible control.

scenes.narration: The longer period also produces Yearly Statistics. An asterisk marks a partial period; the note explains that the report covers only part of it. Do not describe that row as a complete calendar year. Quarterly Statistics adds YTD, the cumulative call count within the report’s included periods for that year. Monthly Statistics uses the same Calls and YTD distinction. October contains five calls. November and December show zero calls while YTD remains five. These are results from available records in the chosen range, not forecasts of future activity.

scenes.title: Apply the same checks across departments
scenes.capture_intent: Show the exact report controls or corresponding actual table described by this contiguous narration span.
scenes.narration: Chicago Fire can review station call distribution; community care and mental-health teams can review operational workload without putting client histories into report notes. Search-and-rescue teams can compare mission-period groups. Security teams can inspect recorded staffing before a patrol review, while wildland coordinators can compare seasonal reporting windows. Industrial teams can examine unit status chronology during a software exercise. In each setting, choose the question, fix the period and scope, inspect the detail rows, and explain missing data before sharing an authorized result.
